description: Width tiers for Health and Physical Education — Foundation Year
subject: Health and Physical Education

generation_rules.notes: Movement standards (M-strand) use task_contexts — width is transferability of skills and capabilities across play and environmental contexts. Health/personal-social standards (P-strand) are mixed: some are concept/understanding standards (phenomena_contexts) and some are capability standards (task_contexts). Axis is specified per standard. All First Nations elaborations included in wider.

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest context in which a student can genuinely be said to have met the descriptor's command term. Not the easiest activity — the minimum honest floor. For Foundation, this typically means one context, one application, one example.
width_notes.typical_width: Full descriptor scope as ACARA intended. Grounded in the range of elaboration cases. Reflects sound standard practice at Foundation — engaged with the descriptor's spirit, not every elaboration.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment directions that add new contexts, phenomena or task types rather than harder versions of the same context. At Foundation, wider often means culturally situated, environmentally varied, or cross-context application. Each item is a discrete direction, not a sub-step.

AC9HPFM01.minimum_width: Practise at least two locomotor skills and one object-manipulation skill in a single play activity or minor game.
AC9HPFM01.typical_width: Practise a range of fundamental movement skills — locomotor, object-manipulation and balance/weight-transfer — across several minor games and play situations; combine skills with basic control and purpose.
wider: Apply fundamental movement skills in natural and outdoor environments, adapting to uneven terrain or open space
Participate in First Nations Australian games (e.g. traditional running or chasing games) and compare their movement demands with other minor games
Combine multiple FMS simultaneously in structured game formats (run–dodge–send) with progressively more complex movement demands
Explore water confidence skills including floating with a buoyancy aid and object retrieval in water
elaborations: applying different locomotor skills to move from one point to another
combining fine and gross motor skills in increasingly complex patterns
sending, controlling and receiving objects at different levels and in different ways
performing a range of water confidence skills such as floating with a buoyancy aid and putting their face in the water
demonstrating how to transfer weight from one part of the body to another
applying fundamental movement skills for purpose and enjoyment in natural environments

AC9HPFM02.minimum_width: Suggest and test at least one alternative way to move or use equipment in a play context; participate in a game with awareness of personal safety (staying within boundaries, using equipment safely).
AC9HPFM02.typical_width: Suggest and test multiple movement approaches in different play situations; make and share judgements about effectiveness and preference; demonstrate spatial awareness in indoor and outdoor environments; follow game safety rules including boundaries and equipment use.
wider: Experiment with movement choices in outdoor and natural settings with varying terrain
Test movement strategies using non-standard equipment (everyday objects, scarves, balloons) to isolate tracking, timing and coordination
Reflect on persistence during challenging movement tasks — linking emotional experience to physical challenge
Design a simple safety rule for a class game, explaining its purpose
elaborations: suggesting and testing different ways to move in a playing space or different ways to use equipment and objects, and making judgements about which are most effective and which movements and equipment they prefer
persisting with challenges and demonstrating resilience while moving their body in a range of situations
participating in games that require them to be aware of personal safety in relation to game boundaries, rules and safe use of equipment
manipulating equipment in a range of different movement situations and tasks, including in minor games, imaginative play and when practising fundamental movement skills
demonstrating spatial awareness when moving around and through indoor and outdoor (natural) environments confidently and safely

AC9HPFM03.minimum_width: Participate in at least one physical activity in an outdoor or natural setting; describe one way physical activity makes them feel.
AC9HPFM03.typical_width: Participate in a range of physical activities in outdoor and natural settings; identify safety strategies for outdoor play; discuss multiple feelings associated with physical activity; identify several opportunities to be active in and around home and community.
wider: Participate in physical activity across a variety of natural environments — grassed areas, bush, beach — adapting movement to the setting
Explore First Nations Australian games traditionally played outdoors, discussing how the setting shapes the game and connecting to cultural belonging
Explore risk and self-regulation strategies for outdoor play (testing footing, staying within safe boundaries, taking considered risks)
Investigate how family or cultural practices shape physical activity opportunities in different communities
elaborations: exploring a range of ways to be active and participate safely in outdoor or natural settings
playing traditional First Nations Australian games and discussing how they are like other games they have experienced
discussing opportunities to be active in spaces in and around their homes
exploring strategies for taking considered risks and developing self-regulation skills when moving and playing in outdoor settings

AC9HPFM04.minimum_width: Follow the rules of one minor game including safety, boundary and equipment rules; identify one example of fair and one example of unfair play.
AC9HPFM04.typical_width: Follow rules and demonstrate fair play across a range of minor games and play situations; identify and describe fair and unfair actions; discuss safety, boundary and equipment rules across different game types.
wider: Participate in First Nations Australian games with their specific rules, discussing how those rules promote fair participation
Discuss scenarios involving intent — accidental vs deliberate — and how this affects judgements about fairness
Connect fair play to emotional impact — how unfair play makes participants feel, linking to emotional literacy work
Lead a brief rule explanation for a peer before beginning a game
elaborations: identifying and describing actions that would constitute fair and unfair play while participating in minor games
demonstrating how to play fairly in a range of minor games and play situations
discussing rules of different games that relate to safety, boundaries and appropriate use of equipment

AC9HPFP01.minimum_width: Share something about who they are (family, culture or personal interest) and identify at least one other type of family structure different from their own.
AC9HPFP01.typical_width: Explore personal identity through stories, discussion and creative expression; make connections between personal qualities, background and belonging; identify and discuss a range of family structures; recognise that everyone has a right to belong and contribute.
wider: Explore identity and belonging stories from First Nations Australian contexts, discussing similarities and differences with students' own experience
Investigate cultural practices from different cultures, including cultures of Asia, that are important to individuals, families and communities
Compare family structures and community roles across First Nations Australian communities
Explore how belonging to different groups (family, class, community) shapes identity and contribution
elaborations: making personal connections with stories that explore identity and belonging; discussing who they are, where they come from and people in their lives
exploring similarities and differences in family structures in First Nations Australian communities and other cultures
exploring cultural practices from different cultures, including the cultures of Asia, that are important to individuals, families and communities
identifying different families in their communities; for example, 2-parent, single-parent, extended and non-traditional families
identifying ways they use their strengths in physical activities to help themselves and others to be successful
recognising that they have a right to belong and contribute to a variety of groups

AC9HPFP02.minimum_width: Identify one disrespectful or hurtful behaviour in a play or story context and suggest a more inclusive alternative; take turns and make one shared decision in a collaborative play activity.
AC9HPFP02.typical_width: Explore stories and scenarios involving exclusion and inclusion; cooperate, collaborate and negotiate in a range of physical activities; explain reasoning in response to challenging social situations; demonstrate respectful interaction consistently.
wider: Explore inclusion and exclusion in stories from different cultural contexts, including First Nations Australian contexts
Practise negotiation in contexts where students must agree on rules or equipment before a game
Reflect on a challenging collaboration experience, identifying what helped the group succeed
Connect respectful social interaction to fair play — practising both simultaneously in game contexts
elaborations: explaining their reasons and actions in response to challenging situations in shared play experiences
identifying characters in texts who have been excluded from a group, exploring why they have been excluded and discussing how other characters could have been more inclusive
cooperating, collaborating and negotiating with others when participating in physical activities to achieve agreed outcomes
identifying behaviours that may be disrespectful and cause hurt or harm to others during play

AC9HPFP03.minimum_width: Name at least four emotions and describe what they look like; use appropriate language or gesture to communicate one feeling in a social or play context.
AC9HPFP03.typical_width: Identify and describe a range of emotions (at least six) in stories, images and peers; connect emotion names with observable indicators (expression, posture, voice); practise appropriate emotional communication in a range of situations; make connections between feelings, body reactions and body language.
wider: Explore emotional expression across different cultural contexts using First Nations Australian or Asian cultural stories and examples
Connect body reactions during physical activity (breathlessness, energy, heart rate) to emotional states
Represent a range of emotions through movement, drawing or other creative expression modes
Explore emotions in adventure and risk stories — connecting emotional responses to physical challenge
elaborations: identifying and describing the emotions of people who are happy, sad, excited, tired, angry, scared or confused
learning and using appropriate language and actions to communicate their feelings in different situations
recalling and sharing emotional responses to different situations and representing these in a variety of ways
reading and viewing stories about adventures, and talking about how characters feel and react when taking risks or responding to emergencies
talking about connections between feelings, body reactions and body language
expressing a variety of emotions, thoughts and views in a range of situations

AC9HPFP04.minimum_width: Identify one situation requiring permission and give a reason why asking matters; practise asking permission in one play or sharing context using respectful language and accepting the response.
AC9HPFP04.typical_width: Explore and explain why permission matters across multiple contexts — possessions, personal space, activity roles; practise seeking, giving and denying permission in play and imaginative contexts; demonstrate respect for 'no' responses; connect bodily autonomy to permission.
wider: Explore permission and consent in physical activity contexts involving personal space (partner games, contact activities)
Practise permission-seeking and denial in role-play scenarios with different outcomes
Discuss digital permission contexts — asking before taking or sharing a photo of someone
Explore negotiation practices in First Nations Australian game and community contexts
elaborations: practising and refining how to ask for permission when sharing possessions or personal space
negotiating roles and demonstrating awareness of rights (such as body autonomy/integrity) and respect for different perspectives through imaginative and shared play experiences
exploring the importance of asking for permission and giving permission when sharing or negotiating in play and respecting someone's right to say no

AC9HPFP05.minimum_width: Name major body parts including private body parts using correct anatomical terms; name two trusted adults; demonstrate one assertive help-seeking strategy in a rehearsed unsafe scenario.
AC9HPFP05.typical_width: Name body parts correctly and articulate bodily autonomy rights; identify a support network of trusted adults across home, school and community; explore and demonstrate protective behaviours and assertive strategies across a range of unsafe/uncomfortable scenarios; recognise online safety and when to seek adult help.
wider: Rehearse help-seeking across varied unsafe scenario types — physical, emotional and online
Explore trusted adult networks in different cultural and community contexts, including First Nations Australian family and community structures
Practise helping a friend who is unsafe — extending help-seeking beyond self-protection
Connect protective behaviours work to digital safety — identifying safe online spaces and trusted adult support for online discomfort
elaborations: exploring protective behaviours and help-seeking strategies they can use when they or others feel unsafe or uncomfortable
exploring and demonstrating assertive strategies to seek help when they or others feel unsafe
recognising online spaces and digital tools that are safe for them to use and recognising the importance of seeking help from a trusted adult if they feel unsafe while online
identifying a support network of adults they can trust to help them if they feel unsafe, uncomfortable or scared
recognising that all people have the right to bodily autonomy: the right to make choices about what others ask them to do with and to their bodies

AC9HPFP06.minimum_width: Identify two health or safety symbols and explain what each means; identify one community safety strategy and describe what it requires them to do.
AC9HPFP06.typical_width: Identify and explain a range of health and safety symbols across home, road, food and water contexts; identify and follow community safety strategies including pedestrian crossings, traffic controllers and pool/beach safety procedures.
wider: Investigate food packaging symbols and labels that indicate healthier choices; discuss how advertising influences food choices
Compare safety strategies across multiple community environments — road, water, home, outdoor — and explain the purpose behind each
Explore safety strategies in natural and outdoor environments, including varied water safety contexts
Connect community safety strategies to personal responsibility — understanding their own role in following and promoting safety
elaborations: identifying household substances that are dangerous and explaining what symbols are used to identify the danger
identifying symbols on food packages that indicate healthier choices
identifying different types of advertising that influence choices about food

exploring different community strategies that keep children safe; for example, pedestrian crossings and traffic lights, safety procedures at swimming pools and beaches, and traffic controllers at school crossings
recognising and following safety symbols and procedures at home and in water and road environments
